## Incident detail

### Phishing, credential theft & BEC

**TI-PH01 — FBI warns of Kali365 PhaaS harvesting M365 OAuth tokens via device-code flow**
`high` · actor: Kali365 phishing-as-a-service operators · impact: High; persistent M365 account takeover, MFA fully bypassed via token capture

The FBI issued a PSA on Kali365, a phishing-as-a-service kit sold on Telegram for as little as $250/month that captures Microsoft 365 OAuth tokens through the legitimate device-code authentication flow. A related year-long device-code campaign logged 218 distinct accounts (~94% corporate mailboxes) between June 2025 and July 2026.

*Examples:* device-code phishing, OAuth token theft, MFA bypass, PhaaS  
*Source:* CSIRT / FBI PSA + The Hacker News  
*Ref:* https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/the-new-phishing-click-how-oauth.html  
*Ref:* https://cyberpress.org/device-code-phishing-bypasses-mfa/  

**TI-PH02 — Misconfigured server exposes three Evilginx operations targeting Microsoft 365**
`high` · actor: unattributed (three distinct Evilginx clusters) · impact: High; AiTM session-token theft on M365, then BEC and account takeover

A misconfigured attacker server revealed three separate phishing operations getting past MFA two mechanically different ways — proxying the live Microsoft login (Evilginx AiTM) and abusing the device-code sign-in flow — each requiring different defenses.

*Examples:* AiTM / reverse-proxy phishing, session hijacking, BEC  
*Source:* OSINT / The Hacker News  
*Ref:* https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/misconfigured-server-reveals-three.html  

### Ransomware & extortion

**TI-RN00 — Storm-2603 deploys Warlock ransomware via SharePoint RCE CVE-2026-45659**
`critical` · `CVE-2026-45659` · **KEV** · actor: Storm-2603 / GOLD SALEM (Warlock ransomware) · impact: High; on-prem SharePoint compromise -> Warlock ransomware + double extortion

The group behind the 2025 ToolShell SharePoint campaign, Storm-2603 (GOLD SALEM, linked by Microsoft to China-based activity), is exploiting on-prem SharePoint RCE CVE-2026-45659 to deploy Warlock ransomware — a repeat of its 2025 on-prem-SharePoint-to-Warlock playbook. CISA KEV-listed Jul 1, 2026.

*Examples:* Warlock ransomware, double extortion, China-nexus  
*Source:* CISA KEV / Microsoft MSTIC + The Hacker News  
*Ref:* https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/sharepoint-rce-cve-2026-45659-added-to.html  
*Ref:* https://hard2bit.com/en/blog/cve-2026-45659-sharepoint-kev-storm2603-warlock/  

**TI-RN02 — FortiBleed stolen-credential campaign feeds INC and Lynx ransomware at 12+ orgs**
`critical` · actor: 'FortiBleed' crew -> INC and Lynx ransomware · impact: High; VPN/firewall foothold converted directly to ransomware deployment

~20 actors under the 'FortiBleed' banner used 74,000 stolen FortiGate firewall/VPN credentials (advertised in June), brute force, and config dumping to break password hashes; the access has already been converted into ransomware at 12+ organizations via the INC and Lynx operations.

*Examples:* stolen credentials, brute force, ransomware deployment  
*Source:* OSINT / BleepingComputer + CybersecurityNews  
*Ref:* https://cybersecuritynews.com/forticlient-ems-instances-exposed-online/  

### Exploitation of internet-facing systems

**TI-EX00 — Microsoft SharePoint Server RCE CVE-2026-45659 under active exploitation (on CISA KEV)**
`critical` · `CVE-2026-45659` · **KEV** · actor: Storm-2603 (GOLD SALEM, China-nexus) · impact: Very high; RCE on internet-facing on-prem SharePoint, used as a network-staging foothold

CISA added CVE-2026-45659 (CVSS 8.8; a low-privilege authenticated RCE in on-prem SharePoint Server) to the KEV catalog on Jul 1, 2026 with a 3-day federal patch deadline (Jul 4). Microsoft had rated exploitation 'less likely' in its May updates, but active exploitation began ~6 weeks later. Remediation: apply the May 2026 updates (KB5002863/68/70), prioritising internet-facing servers.

*Examples:* deserialization RCE, on-prem SharePoint, mass exploitation, network staging  
*Source:* CISA KEV / Microsoft MSTIC + The Hacker News  
*Ref:* https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/sharepoint-rce-cve-2026-45659-added-to.html  
*Ref:* https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2025/07/22/disrupting-active-exploitation-of-on-premises-sharepoint-vulnerabilities/  

**TI-EX01 — Joomla iCagenda & Balbooa Forms zero-days added to CISA KEV (arbitrary file upload RCE)**
`critical` · `CVE-2026-48939` · **KEV** · actor: automated mass-exploitation clusters · impact: Very high; unauth file upload -> PHP code execution on internet-facing Joomla sites

CISA added two max-severity Joomla flaws to the KEV catalog after zero-day exploitation: CVE-2026-48939 (iCagenda arbitrary file upload -> PHP code exec, abused since Jun 15, 2026 in automated attacks) and CVE-2026-56291 (Balbooa Forms upload -> RCE). Related Joomla builder flaws (JoomShaper CVE-2026-48908, Joomlack CVE-2026-56290) followed.

*Examples:* arbitrary file upload, unauthenticated RCE, mass exploitation  
*Source:* CISA KEV / The Hacker News  
*Ref:* https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/icagenda-and-balbooa-forms-joomla-flaws.html  
*Ref:* https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/07/10/cisa-adds-two-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog  

### Software supply-chain & SDLC compromise

**TI-SC02 — 'Shai-Hulud' self-propagating worm hits 170+ npm & PyPI packages again**
`critical` · actor: unattributed (self-propagating npm/PyPI worm) · impact: Very high; worm-style spread through dependency graphs, secret harvesting at install

A fresh Shai-Hulud wave compromised 170+ packages across npm and PyPI, harvesting secrets during install and re-publishing itself through maintainers' own tokens to spread — the same worm pattern that hit the ecosystem earlier in 2026, now recurring.

*Examples:* self-propagating worm, install hooks, token theft & re-publish  
*Source:* CSIRT / OX Security + Unit 42  
*Ref:* https://www.ox.security/blog/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-170-packages-hit-across-npm-pypi/  
*Ref:* https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/monitoring-npm-supply-chain-attacks/  

**TI-SC01 — 17 fake payment SDKs on npm & PyPI harvest CI/CD secrets to an ngrok C2**
`high` · actor: unattributed (coordinated registry-malware actor) · impact: Very high; one install reaches CI/CD, cloud, and developer secrets

On Jul 7, 2026 a threat actor published 17 malicious packages (13 npm + 4 PyPI) impersonating Paysafe, Skrill, and Neteller SDKs. Each harvested API keys, AWS credentials, GitHub/npm tokens, and secret-looking env vars, exfiltrating to a C2 hidden behind an ngrok tunnel; sandbox-evasion checks bailed on <2 CPU cores. Detected malicious within ~6 minutes of publication.

*Examples:* typosquat / brandjacking, install-time credential theft, sandbox evasion  
*Source:* CSIRT / GBHackers + ComplianceHub  
*Ref:* https://gbhackers.com/npm-and-pypi-malware/  
*Ref:* https://compliancehub.wiki/npm-pypi-stealer-packages-payment-apps-supply-chain-2026/  

### Cloud, SaaS & API abuse

**TI-CL01 — Salesloft Drift OAuth token theft (UNC6395 'Icarus') drains 700+ Salesforce tenants**
`critical` · actor: UNC6395 / 'Icarus' (overlaps ShinyHunters activity) · impact: Very high; SaaS data + embedded plaintext AWS/Snowflake/VPN credentials across 700+ orgs

Between Jun 8-18, 2026 attackers used OAuth tokens issued to the Salesloft Drift app to reach 700+ Salesforce customer instances via API and systematically export support cases, contacts, and — critically — plaintext AWS keys, Snowflake tokens, and VPN credentials embedded in that data. Microsoft has since mapped three Salesforce attack paths tied to a year of ShinyHunters activity.

*Examples:* OAuth token abuse, connected-app compromise, secondary credential harvest  
*Source:* CSIRT / Google Cloud (Mandiant) + Microsoft  
*Ref:* https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/data-theft-salesforce-instances-via-salesloft-drift  
*Ref:* https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/microsoft-maps-year-long-shinyhunters.html  

**TI-CL02 — Klue integration breach exposes Salesforce CRM data via stolen OAuth tokens**
`high` · actor: 'Icarus' extortion group · impact: Medium-to-high; CRM data theft through a trusted third-party connector

On Jun 12, 2026 attackers used a compromised legacy integration credential to obtain OAuth tokens connecting Klue to Salesforce and other platforms, then pulled customer CRM data; Salesforce disabled the Klue integration in response. The Icarus group, active since April 2026, is behind it.

*Examples:* third-party integration abuse, OAuth token theft, SaaS supply chain  
*Source:* OSINT / CSO Online + Hackread  
*Ref:* https://www.csoonline.com/article/4187907/klue-breach-exposed-salesforce-crm-data-through-stolen-oauth-tokens.html  
*Ref:* https://hackread.com/salesforce-disables-klue-integration-oauth-token-data/  

### AI, LLM & agentic-system attacks

**TI-AI01 — Langflow authorization-bypass CVE-2026-55255 added to CISA KEV (agentic AI builder)**
`critical` · `CVE-2026-55255` · **KEV** · actor: opportunistic exploitation · impact: High; auth bypass on an internet-exposed low-code AI/agent-building platform

CISA added CVE-2026-55255, an Authorization-Bypass-Through-User-Controlled-Key flaw in Langflow (a popular low-code framework for building LLM/agent workflows), to the KEV catalog after active exploitation — a reminder that the AI tooling layer itself is now internet-facing attack surface.

*Examples:* authorization bypass, AI-infra exploitation, user-controlled key  
*Source:* CISA KEV / vendor advisory  
*Ref:* https://senserva.com/exploited-this-week.html  
*Ref:* https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog  

**TI-AI03 — MCP server exploits: MCPJam Inspector RCE CVE-2026-23744 (9.8); GitHub MCP data exfil**
`critical` · `CVE-2026-23744` · actor: research-demonstrated + in-the-wild reuse · impact: High; RCE on agent tooling and private-repo exfil via poisoned MCP inputs

The Model Context Protocol layer is now a live target: CVE-2026-23744 gave attackers RCE on MCPJam Inspector (CVSS 9.8), a booby-trapped PDF tripped a physical pump via a Claude MCP link, and attackers abused GitHub's MCP server to exfiltrate private repository data through malicious issues — the harness/tooling seam, not the model, is the weak point.

*Examples:* MCP tool poisoning, remote code execution, zero-click exfil  
*Source:* CSIRT / advisory + arXiv  
*Ref:* https://botmonster.com/posts/ai-coding-agent-insider-threat-prompt-injection-mcp-exploits/  
*Ref:* https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.21392
